providers.title: Drawings and the crossing number
providers.scope: Vertices at distinct points, edges as simple arcs whose interiors avoid the vertices and meet in finitely many proper crossings of two edges; cr(G) is the least number of crossing points.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Zarankiewicz's formula (OpenAI)
providers.scope: cr(K_{m,n}) = d_m d_n with d_r = floor(r/2) floor((r-1)/2). Proved in the lesson The Zarankiewicz formula. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Harary-Hill formula (OpenAI)
providers.scope: cr(K_n) = Z(n) = d_n d_(n-2)/4 for n >= 3. Proved in the lesson Two-page drawings and the Harary-Hill formula. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Polynomials vanishing on open sets
providers.scope: A real polynomial vanishing on a nonempty open set is zero, so finitely many nonzero polynomials have a common nonzero point in every nonempty open set. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Zarankiewicz's drawing
providers.scope: K_{m,n} has a straight-line drawing with exactly d_m d_n crossing points, so cr(K_{m,n}) <= d_m d_n. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Normal drawings
providers.scope: Polygonal, straight near every vertex and crossing point, and without crossings of edges with a common endpoint.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Normalization (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Every drawing can be replaced by a normal drawing with no more crossing points; cr(G) is attained by a normal drawing. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Polygonal paths in open sets
providers.scope: A continuous path in an open subset of the plane can be replaced by a polygonal walk in it with the same ends. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Removing loops
providers.scope: A polygonal walk between distinct points contains a polygonal arc between them. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: From arcs to polygons
providers.scope: Every drawing has a polygonal drawing with no more crossing points that is straight near its vertices and crossing points. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: One exchange
providers.scope: If two edges with a common endpoint cross, exchanging their initial parts and removing loops gives a drawing with fewer crossing points. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Four endpoints
providers.scope: In a normal drawing every crossing point lies on two edges with four distinct endpoints. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Simple cycles span the cycle space
providers.scope: The cycle space of a graph is spanned by the signed edge vectors of oriented simple cycles. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The form J
providers.scope: J(e,f) = I(e,f) + (1/2) sum over common endpoints v of sigma_v(e) sigma_v(f) T_v(e,f), with I the signed number of crossings and T_v the order sign from a cut at v.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cycle pairing (OpenAI)
providers.scope: In every normal drawing, for all orientations and cuts, J(z,y) = 0 for any two cycles z, y. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Triangles
providers.scope: The boundary of a triangle and a closed polygonal walk in general position have signed intersection zero. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Closed polygonal walks
providers.scope: Two closed polygonal walks in general position have signed intersection zero. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Two chords in a disc
providers.scope: The signed intersection of two directed chords with four distinct endpoints is half the sum of the products of endpoint coefficients and order signs from any cut. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Lagrange interpolation
providers.scope: A polynomial of degree at most N-1 is determined by its values at N distinct nodes, by the Lagrange formula. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Barycentric weights
providers.scope: The sum of A(u_p)/G'(u_p) over N distinct nodes is the coefficient of t^(N-1) in A, so it vanishes when deg A <= N-2. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Dividing by a linear factor
providers.scope: A polynomial in two variables vanishing on a line u = c or v = c is divisible by u - c or v - c, with the degree bounds lowered by one. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The odd pattern (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For distinct x_1, ..., x_(2s+1), evaluation at (x_p, x_q), (p,q) in the two-triangle pattern Q_s, is a bijection from the polynomials of degree at most s-1 in each variable onto R^(Q_s). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The even pattern (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For s >= 2 and distinct u_1, ..., u_(2s), evaluation on the pattern L_s is a bijection from P_(s-1,s-2) and from P_(s-2,s-1) onto R^(L_s). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Rank at special points
providers.scope: A polynomial matrix of rank at most r at infinitely many points has rank at most r everywhere. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Rank loss and multiple roots
providers.scope: If a square polynomial matrix of size k has rank at most k-q at t_0, then (xi - t_0)^q divides its determinant. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Subspace intersection inequality (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If U_i cap V_i = 0 for i = 1, ..., m in a real space of dimension N, then the sum of dim(U_i cap V_j) over all i, j is at most floor(m^2/4) N. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Sharpness
providers.scope: Two complementary subspaces and two groups of indices attain the bound floor(m^2/4) N.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Ranks of differences (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If X_i - Y_i is invertible for d x d matrices, i = 1, ..., m, then the sum of rank(X_i - Y_j) over i != j is at least 2 d_m d. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Blocks of a drawing of K_{m,n}
providers.scope: In a normal drawing, the diagonal block J^{ii} is half the sign matrix of the order of the edges at a_i, and an off-diagonal entry of J^{ik} with p != q is a signed crossing count. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Block relation (OpenAI)
providers.scope: J^{ik} - J^{i1} - J^{1k} + J^{11} is additive (of the form r_p + c_q). Uses the cycle pairing.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The detector (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For n = 2s+1 the interpolation map Phi kills additive and diagonal matrices, has rank at most one per nonzero off-diagonal entry, and maps the sign matrix of every linear order to an invertible matrix. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Odd n (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For n odd, every normal drawing of K_{m,n} has at least d_m d_n pairs of independent edges with nonzero signed crossing count, hence at least d_m d_n crossings. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Even n
providers.scope: For n even, cr(K_{m,n}) >= d_m d_n, by deleting one vertex of the second class at a time. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Zarankiewicz's formula (OpenAI)
providers.scope: cr(K_{m,n}) = d_m d_n for all m, n >= 1. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Polynomial cycle tests (OpenAI)
providers.scope: In a normal drawing of K_n, the sum of J([ip],[kq]) w_i w_p w_k w_q H(t_i,t_p,t_k,t_q) vanishes for every polynomial H of degree at most n-2 in each variable. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Order pairing (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For 2s nodes and any linear order, the weighted order pairing is nondegenerate on P_(s-1,s-2) x P_(s-2,s-1). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Injectivity (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For n = 2s+1, evaluating symmetric polynomials of degree at most s-2 in each variable at the ordered pairs of independent edges with nonzero signed crossing count is injective. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Odd n (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For n = 2s+1 >= 5, every normal drawing of K_n has at least Z(n) pairs of independent edges with nonzero signed crossing count, hence at least Z(n) crossings. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The lower bound (OpenAI)
providers.scope: cr(K_n) >= Z(n) for every n >= 3. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Two semicircles
providers.scope: Semicircles over the axis in one half-plane cross exactly when their endpoints alternate, once and properly, and semicircles with one common endpoint meet only there. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The two-page drawing
providers.scope: With suitable positions on the spine, the semicircle drawing of K_n with edges up or down by the endpoint sum modulo n is a drawing whose crossings are the same-colour alternating pairs. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The count (OpenAI)
providers.scope: The endpoint-sum two-page drawing of K_n has exactly Z(n) crossing points. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Harary-Hill formula (OpenAI)
providers.scope: cr(K_n) = Z(n) for every n >= 3. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
